tldr: Foundry hosted agents can now enforce outbound network rules, a necessary control before deploying agents that call external services.
A reported $22,000 Marketplace bill shows that Azure sponsorship credits may not cover third-party models such as Claude; verify billing boundaries before deployment.
WSO2 Agent Manager is now generally available as an open-source control plane for agent identity, security and lifecycle management across environments.

top.title: Foundry adds outbound network controls for hosted agents
top.summary: Microsoft Foundry's hosted agents can now use ordered allow and deny rules for outbound destinations, including wildcard FQDNs such as *.contoso.com.
top.why: Use this preview to replace unrestricted agent egress with an explicit allowlist before agents are trusted with production data or tools.

top.title: Foundry Routines automate scheduled and event-driven agents
top.summary: Foundry Agent Service now previews Foundry Routines, a native trigger primitive for running published agents on schedules or in response to business events.
top.why: This can remove separate scheduler and event-orchestration components, but you should still design for retries, duplicate events and run-level cost controls.

top.title: Azure sponsorship customer reports an unexpected $22,000 Claude bill
top.summary: An Azure Community customer reports that Claude deployments through Azure AI Foundry generated a roughly $22,000 Marketplace charge despite the organisation expecting Azure Sponsorship credits to cover its usage.
top.why: Treat third-party model billing as a separate cost boundary and confirm sponsorship, Marketplace and budget-alert coverage before enabling production inference.

top.title: Foundry agents gain GA enable and disable controls in Agent 365
top.summary: Microsoft Foundry agents can now be enabled or disabled from the Agent 365 governance surface in Microsoft Admin Center.
top.why: This gives administrators a central emergency and lifecycle control, so include agent disablement in operational runbooks and access reviews.

top.title: PostgreSQL 18 reaches Azure elastic clusters
top.summary: Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support PostgreSQL 18 for distributed, cloud-scale workloads.
top.why: Teams planning a PostgreSQL 18 migration can consider the elastic-cluster option, but should validate extension, compatibility and distributed-query behaviour first.

also.title: Foundry agents can now publish to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams
also.summary: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now generally available, providing a native route to end users.

also.title: Azure adds a replication-slot sync metric for PostgreSQL
also.summary: A new Azure Monitor metric reports the synchronization status of logical replication slots on PostgreSQL Flexible Server.

also.title: Azure previews guided Copilot app building in VS Code
also.summary: A structured GitHub Copilot workflow in VS Code guides users from an application idea through deployment to Azure instead of relying on free-form chat.

top.title: Researchers used Claude to reach OpenAI's GitHub repository
top.summary: Security researchers reportedly used Claude to compromise an OpenAI employee account and access sensitive GitHub data, demonstrating that an AI coding assistant can materially accelerate an intrusion.
top.why: Treat agentic coding tools as privileged production identities: enforce least privilege, isolate repositories and require human approval for credentials and high-impact actions.

top.title: Anthropic opens a robot-powered biology research lab
top.summary: Anthropic has opened a San Francisco Bay Area wet lab where robots will automate biology tasks using Claude models, although the specific research projects remain unclear.
top.why: This is a notable move from selling models toward operating model-driven physical systems, raising the importance of isolation, tool permissions and auditable workflows in AI hosting designs.

top.title: AI hallucination nearly triggered a US military operation
top.summary: A report says an AI system incorrectly identified Chinese nuclear components and nearly contributed to a military operation, underscoring the danger of treating generated intelligence as verified fact.
top.why: For high-consequence workloads, require source grounding, confidence and uncertainty signals, and human confirmation rather than allowing an LLM output to trigger action directly.

top.title: Virginia moves to give communities more control over data centers
top.summary: Virginia's governor ordered an AI task force and measures that could increase local influence over data-center development and slow approvals; the order also bans executive-branch nondisclosure agreements.
top.why: If your capacity plan depends on Virginia, add permitting, power and community-approval risk to the assumptions behind GPU and regional expansion decisions.

top.title: PrismML launches a 27B ternary model for local hardware
top.summary: PrismML announced Bonsai 2 27B, a multimodal model based on Qwen3.8 27B that uses ternary compression and is claimed to fit on PCs and some high-end mobile devices.
top.why: Evaluate this class of compressed model for private or edge inference where lower hosting and data-transfer costs matter, while independently checking quality and hardware requirements.

also.title: OpenAI documents warned that its web strategy could create a 'doom loop'
also.summary: Unsealed documents in The New York Times' case describe internal concerns that OpenAI and Microsoft's scraping and AI-search strategy could damage the web ecosystem.

also.title: FAA plans an $875 million AI traffic-congestion system
also.summary: The FAA is preparing an $875 million AI system to manage Washington-area air traffic congestion before considering a nationwide rollout.

also.title: OpenAI proposes a six-pillar youth safety blueprint in Australia
also.summary: OpenAI published an Australian Youth Safety Blueprint describing six areas for protecting and empowering young people using AI services.

top.title: WSO2 Agent Manager reaches GA for cross-platform agent governance
top.summary: WSO2 Agent Manager is now generally available as an open-source platform for centralised governance, identity management, security controls and operational oversight across models, agent frameworks and deployment environments.
top.why: Evaluate it as a control-plane alternative to building separate agent registries, identity integrations and policy tooling, while verifying its Azure and enterprise-operations fit.

top.title: DoorDash reports measurable results from multi-agent flag cleanup
top.summary: DoorDash used multiple agents, MCP, isolated Git worktrees, engineer approval and automated validation across 60,000 flags and 623 repositories; 45 of 50 evaluated flags produced usable pull requests at an average of 13.8 minutes and $4.79 each.
top.why: The concrete cost and success rate provide a useful benchmark for deciding whether agent automation is economical for repetitive repository-maintenance work.

top.title: MariaDB 13 reaches GA with Oracle compatibility changes
top.summary: MariaDB Community Server 13.0 is generally available with expanded procedural SQL and DML capabilities, observability improvements, performance changes and new deprecations.
top.why: If MariaDB backs an AI application or agent service, review the deprecations and compatibility changes before adopting the new major version in shared production infrastructure.

also.title: Open-weight models now produce most Vercel AI Gateway tokens
also.summary: The report says open-weight models account for a majority of tokens on Vercel's AI Gateway, while Anthropic still represents 64% of spending.

also.title: Kubernetes inference deployments need better cost accounting
also.summary: The article examines why Kubernetes can run AI inference without necessarily exposing the full GPU, utilisation and per-request cost of that workload.

also.title: Buildpacks are presented as a way to scale container security controls
also.summary: The article argues that standardised buildpacks can make container security controls more consistently enforceable across many services.
